title: From Temples to Duty-Free | The Ancient History of Modern Perfume
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的知识，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today, we are going to be talking about the history of perfume.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将探讨香水的历史。

sentences.en: It is a curious story that takes us from Ancient Mesopotamia to the Middle East, from southern France to modern airport terminals.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引人入胜的故事，带我们从古代的美索不达米亚走到中东，从法国南部走到现代的机场航站楼。

sentences.en: So, I hope you’ll enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 所以，希望你会喜欢。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about the history of perfume.
sentences.zh: 那么好，我们直接切入正题，聊聊香水的历史。

sentences.en: As any language learner knows, some words are best left in their original version, not translated.
sentences.zh: 正如任何语言学习者所知，有些词最好保留原汁原味，不要翻译。

sentences.en: This is certainly true with French, a language people have long associated with beauty, sophistication, and elegance.
sentences.zh: 对于法语来说绝对如此，人们长期以来一直把这门语言与美丽、精致和优雅联系在一起。

sentences.en: And perhaps nowhere is it more true than when it comes to French words relating to something that France is rightfully very proud of: perfume.
sentences.zh: 而且，当涉及法国引以为傲的事物——香水——相关的法语词汇时，这一点尤其正确。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the small town in southern France that is the perfume capital of the world: Grasse.
sentences.zh: 以法国南部那个被称为世界香水之都的小镇为例：格拉斯（Grasse）。

sentences.en: A name that evokes the fields of lavender and jasmine used in the world’s finest fragrances.
sentences.zh: 这个名字让人联想到世界上最优质香水所使用的薰衣草和茉莉花田。

sentences.en: But if you translate it into English? Well… Grasse just means “fat.”
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它翻译成英文呢？嗯……Grasse 的意思只是“脂肪”。

sentences.en: And what about the title given to the greatest perfumers—the masters of scent, the artists who create the most luxurious fragrances in the world?
sentences.zh: 那么，授予那些最伟大的调香师——气味大师、创造世界上最奢华香水的艺术家们的头衔是什么呢？

sentences.en: In French, they are called “grands nez”—which means “great nose.”
sentences.zh: 在法语中，他们被称为“grands nez”——意思是“大鼻子”。

sentences.en: Or, if you were being particularly uncharitable, you might translate it as… “big nose.”
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你特别刻薄的话，你也可以把它翻译成……“大鼻子”。

sentences.en: We’ll come to learn more about what it takes to become a “big nose”, or rather a “grand nez”, later on in the episode, but first, we must wind the clocks back and talk about the early days of perfume.
sentences.zh: 我们将在节目后面进一步了解成为“大鼻子”（或者更准确地说是“grand nez”）需要什么，但首先，我们要把时钟拨回过去，聊聊香水的早期历史。

sentences.en: And these early days were early indeed. The tradition of creating a scent and either covering your body in it or spraying it around a room goes back much further than modern France, further than Rome, and even further than the pyramids of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 而这段早期历史确实非常古老。创造一种气味并将其涂抹在身上或喷洒在房间里的传统，其历史比现代法国要久远得多，比罗马更久远，甚至比埃及的金字塔还要久远。

sentences.en: Some of the earliest evidence of creating scents dates back more than 4,000 years to Mesopotamia, in modern-day Iraq.
sentences.zh: 一些最早的香水制造证据可以追溯到 4,000 多年前位于现今伊拉克的美索不达米亚。

sentences.en: And, from the very beginning, it had two purposes.
sentences.zh: 而且，从一开始，它就有两个目的。

sentences.en: The first was ritualistic; people burned aromatic resins, woods, and spices as offerings to their gods.
sentences.zh: 第一个是宗教仪式性质的；人们燃烧芳香树脂、木材和香料作为对神的供奉。

sentences.en: The idea was simple: if something smelled heavenly, it was probably appreciated by the heavens.
sentences.zh: 这个想法很简单：如果某种东西闻起来像天堂一样香，那么神灵可能也会喜欢。

sentences.en: The other, well, it was for a far more practical reason.
sentences.zh: 至于另一个，嗯，则是出于一个更加实际的原因。

sentences.en: Today we live in a world where most people have showers in their houses, soap is cheap, deodorant is everywhere, and there really is no valid reason to not wash yourself regularly.
sentences.zh: 今天我们生活在一个大多数人家里都有淋浴、肥皂很便宜、除臭剂随处可见的世界里，不经常洗澡确实没有什么合理的理由。

sentences.en: But clearly, this is a relatively modern phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，这相对来说是一个现代现象。

sentences.en: Go back a few centuries—or even just 100 years—and the world was a much smellier place.
sentences.zh: 把时间倒回几个世纪——甚至仅仅 100 年前——世界要臭得多。

sentences.en: Without modern hygiene, strong body odours were just a part of life.
sentences.zh: 在没有现代卫生条件的情况下，强烈的体味只是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Sweat, unwashed clothes, the lingering scent of livestock or open sewage in the streets, it was all unavoidable, the world was just smellier.
sentences.zh: 汗水、没洗过的衣服、挥之不去的牲畜气味或街上露天下水道的味道，这些都是不可避免的，世界就是这么臭。

sentences.en: And so, perfume wasn’t just about smelling nice, it was about covering up reality.
sentences.zh: 因此，香水不仅是为了闻起来好闻，更是为了掩盖现实。

sentences.en: So, how were these early perfumes created?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些早期的香水是如何制作的呢？

sentences.en: Well, the process was not too dissimilar to modern perfume making.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个过程与现代香水的制作并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: They would extract the fragrant oils from flowers, resins, and spices, and distil them to leave only the best-smelling scents.
sentences.zh: 他们从花朵、树脂和香料中提取芳香精油，并将其蒸馏，只留下气味最好的成分。

sentences.en: These scents were often used as religious offerings, both being burned in temples, and with priests dousing themselves with them during ceremonies, scents like frankincense and myrrh, which you might remember as being gifts the Three Kings brought to the baby Jesus.
sentences.zh: 这些香味经常被用作宗教祭品，既在神庙中燃烧，又在仪式上由祭司们洒在自己身上，比如乳香和没药，你可能还记得那是东方三博士送给小耶稣的礼物。

sentences.en: But perfume wasn’t just for the gods; it was also for the living, a way to have pleasant scents that followed you everywhere you went.
sentences.zh: 但香水不仅属于神灵，也属于活人，它是一种无论走到哪里都能随身携带怡人香气的方式。

sentences.en: And perhaps nowhere was this more true than in Ancient Egypt, where perfume became a serious status symbol.
sentences.zh: 而且，也许没有哪个地方比古埃及更能体现这一点了，在那里，香水成为了身份的象征。

sentences.en: For the Egyptians, scent was as important as gold or fine clothing.
sentences.zh: 对于埃及人来说，气味和黄金或华丽的衣服一样重要。

sentences.en: The wealthy bathed in perfumed oils, covered their wigs in fragrant wax, and carried scented cones on their heads that would melt throughout the day, slowly releasing pleasant aromas.
sentences.zh: 富人们用香油沐浴，在假发上涂抹香蜡，头上顶着香锥，这些香锥会在一整天里融化，慢慢散发出宜人的芳香。

sentences.en: One theory about why perfume became particularly popular in Egypt is one that you might have guessed.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么香水在埃及变得如此受欢迎，有一个你可能已经猜到了的理论。

sentences.en: Egypt is hot! A burning desert sun, long, sweaty days, and—like everywhere else in the ancient world—no soap, no deodorant, and no running water.
sentences.zh: 埃及天气炎热！火辣的沙漠太阳、漫长而汗流浃背的日子，而且——就像古代世界的其他地方一样——没有肥皂、没有除臭剂，也没有自来水。

sentences.en: Sure, as a wealthy and status-seeking Egyptian, you might have had people fanning you down and carrying you around in a chariot so you didn’t have to break a sweat, but if you wanted to avoid smelling too much like an overworked donkey, perfume was essential.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一个富裕且追求地位的埃及人，你可能会让人给你扇风，用战车抬着你四处走动，这样你就不用出一身汗了，但如果你想避免闻起来太像一头过度劳累的驴，香水是必不可少的。

sentences.en: And even the dead wore perfume. The mummification process involved covering bodies in frankincense, myrrh, and aromatic oils, not just for preservation, but so that the dead would smell divine in the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 甚至死者也使用香水。木乃伊制作过程包括将尸体涂上乳香、没药和芳香油，不仅为了防腐，还为了让死者在来世闻起来像神一样芬芳。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there was Cleopatra.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然还有克利奥帕特拉（Cleopatra）。

sentences.en: She is said to have been obsessed with perfume.
sentences.zh: 据说她对香水着迷至极。

sentences.en: When she sailed to meet Mark Antony, so the legend goes, she had the sails of her boat soaked in perfume so that long before he saw her, he could smell her.
sentences.zh: 传说她乘船去见马克·安东尼（Mark Antony）时，让人把船帆浸泡在香水里，这样远在他看到她之前，就能闻到她的气味。

sentences.en: It’s a dramatic story, perhaps not one based in any historical truth, but it is also a clever reminder of the power of scent: to create an impression, to seduce, and to linger in someone’s mind long after you’ve left the room.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满戏剧性的故事，或许并没有什么历史依据，但它也是一个巧妙的提醒，展现了气味的力量：留下印象、诱惑他人，并在你离开房间后很久依然萦绕在人们的脑海中。

sentences.en: By the way, if you’d like to learn more about the fascinating life of Cleopatra, episode 461 is the one for you.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你想更多地了解克利奥帕特拉传奇的一生，第 461 期节目就是为你准备的。

sentences.en: But, if the Egyptians perfected the art of perfume, the Romans took its use to the extreme.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果说埃及人完善了香水艺术，罗马人则将香水的使用推向了极致。

sentences.en: Romans bathed in scented waters, and doused their clothes, furniture, and even their horses in fragrance.
sentences.zh: 罗马人用带香味的水沐浴，并在衣服、家具甚至马匹上喷洒香水。

sentences.en: Some even had perfume fountains at their extravagant banquets, spraying scented mist over their guests.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至在他们奢侈的宴会上设置了香水喷泉，向客人们喷洒带香味的雾气。

sentences.en: And, of course, perfume had a very practical function in Rome, because, once again, people smelled bad.
sentences.zh: 当然，香水在罗马有着非常实用的功能，因为，再次说明，那时候的人们体味很难闻。

sentences.en: Public baths helped, but let’s not forget that Roman cities had open sewers, unwashed togas, and streets filled with animals.
sentences.zh: 公共浴场有所帮助，但别忘了罗马城市里有露天的下水道、没洗过的托加长袍以及到处都是动物的街道。

sentences.en: If you were wealthy, you covered yourself in perfume to stand apart from the sweaty, unwashed masses.
sentences.zh: 如果你很富有，你就会浑身喷满香水，以此来与那些满身大汗、不洗澡的底层民众区分开来。

sentences.en: In fact, perfume became so popular in Rome that it started to be imported from all over the world: Arabian myrrh, Indian cinnamon, and North African flowers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，香水在罗马变得如此受欢迎，以至于开始从世界各地进口：阿拉伯的没药、印度的肉桂和北非的花朵。

sentences.en: It was a booming industry, and the average Roman senator’s daily perfume consumption would probably even put a member of the Kardashian family to shame.
sentences.zh: 这是一个蓬勃发展的行业，平均一个罗马参议员每天消耗的香水，大概会让卡戴珊（Kardashian）家族的成员都感到汗颜。

sentences.en: But with the fall of the Roman Empire, perfume’s prominence faded in much of Europe, at least for a while.
sentences.zh: 但随着罗马帝国的衰落，香水在欧洲大部分地区的显赫地位黯然失色，至少有一段时间是这样。

sentences.en: While Europe “forgot” about perfume for several centuries, the Middle East became its new home.
sentences.zh: 当欧洲“忘记”香水好几个世纪时，中东成为了它的新家园。

sentences.en: During the Islamic Golden Age, from the 8th to the 13th centuries, Arabic and Persian scientists revolutionised the way perfumes were made.
sentences.zh: 在公元 8 世纪到 13 世纪的伊斯兰黄金时代，阿拉伯和波斯的科学家革新了香水的制作方法。

sentences.en: They perfected distillation, which is a technique that allowed for the extraction of pure, concentrated scents, and is still a method used in modern perfume-making.
sentences.zh: 他们完善了蒸馏技术，这是一种能够提取纯净、浓缩香味的技术，至今仍是现代香水制造中使用的方法。

sentences.en: And from here, from the Middle East, the knowledge of perfume spread back into Europe, carried along trade routes from the Middle East to Italy, Spain, and to the country that would become the spiritual home of perfume, France.
sentences.zh: 从这里，从中东，关于香水的知识传回了欧洲，沿着从中东到意大利、西班牙的贸易路线，传到了将成为香水精神故乡的国家——法国。

sentences.en: If you were to ask someone today which country is most associated with perfume, the answer would almost certainly be France.
sentences.zh: 如果你今天问别人哪个国家与香水的联系最紧密，答案几乎肯定是法国。

sentences.en: And it is a well-deserved reputation. Because while the Romans indulged in excess, and the Middle East perfected the science, it was in France that perfume became an art form.
sentences.zh: 而且这个声誉实至名归。因为虽然罗马人沉溺于穷奢极欲，中东人完善了科学，但正是在法国，香水变成了一门艺术。

sentences.en: But why France? And why Grasse, the small town you heard about at the start of the episode that still calls itself the perfume capital of the world?
sentences.zh: 但为什么是法国？为什么是格拉斯？就是你在节目开始时听到的那个至今仍自称世界香水之都的小镇？

sentences.en: Well, strangely enough, it all comes down to leather gloves.
sentences.zh: 说来奇怪，这一切都归结于皮手套。

sentences.en: In the 16th century, Grasse was famous for its glove-making industry.
sentences.zh: 在 16 世纪，格拉斯以其手套制造业而闻名。

sentences.en: But there was one problem: they smelled terrible.
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题：它们闻起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: This was real leather, made from the skin of dead cows, and as anyone who has ever spent any time at a tannery will know, the process of making leather smells very bad.
sentences.zh: 这是真正的皮革，由死牛的皮制成，正如任何在制革厂待过的人所知，制作皮革的过程闻起来非常难闻。

sentences.en: So, local artisans began scenting the gloves with floral extracts to mask the unpleasant odour, to hide the nasty smell.
sentences.zh: 因此，当地的工匠开始用花卉提取物给手套加香，以掩盖难闻的气味，隐藏刺鼻的臭味。

sentences.en: This small innovation led to a huge transformation.
sentences.zh: 这一小小的创新带来了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: The demand for scented products grew, and soon, combined with increased taxes on leather, Grasse’s leather industry faded away, replaced by something far more profitable: perfume.
sentences.zh: 对带香味产品的需求不断增长，很快，加上皮革税的增加，格拉斯的皮革工业逐渐消亡，取而代之的是一项利润高得多的产业：香水。

sentences.en: And by the time of King Louis XIV, in the late 17th and early 18th century, perfume was no longer just a luxury; it was a necessity at the royal court.
sentences.zh: 到了 17 世纪末和 18 世纪初的法国国王路易十四（Louis XIV）时期，香水不再仅仅是一种奢侈品，它成了王室宫廷中的必需品。

sentences.en: The King of France was famously obsessed with fragrance, and the halls of his palace at Versailles were filled with the smells of perfumed waters, scented gloves, and aromatic balls.
sentences.zh: 这位法国国王以痴迷香水而闻名，他凡尔赛宫的走廊里弥漫着香水、香手套和香球的气味。

sentences.en: At a time when bathing was still rare, perfume became a way of covering up unpleasant realities, not just for individuals, but for entire rooms.
sentences.zh: 在那个洗澡仍然很少见的时代，香水成为了一种掩盖令人不快现实的方式，不仅对个人而言是这样，对整个房间也是如此。

sentences.en: Fountains in Versailles were filled with orange blossom water, and royal furniture was sprayed with lavender and rose extracts.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛宫的喷泉里注满了橙花水，皇家家具上喷洒了薰衣草和玫瑰提取物。

sentences.en: And it was during this time that the modern perfume industry began to take shape.
sentences.zh: 正是在这段时间里，现代香水产业开始成形。

sentences.en: Perfumers in Grasse and Paris began refining their distillation techniques, using alcohol instead of oil to create lighter, more wearable fragrances.
sentences.zh: 格拉斯和巴黎的调香师开始改进他们的蒸馏技术，用酒精代替油来创造更轻盈、更易佩戴的香水。

sentences.en: These would be packaged up into beautiful little bottles, not too dissimilar to the stylised bottles that perfume comes in today.
sentences.zh: 这些香水将被装进美丽的精美小瓶子里，与今天香水采用的时尚瓶子相差无几。

sentences.en: And by the 18th and 19th centuries, perfume was no longer just for royalty; it was for anyone who could afford it.
sentences.zh: 到了 18 世纪和 19 世纪，香水不再只是皇室的专利，它属于任何买得起的人。

sentences.en: Still, it was not cheap, but it became something that was available not just for a king.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它并不便宜，但它已经不再是帝王将相的专属。

sentences.en: And this brings us to a big question: why is perfume still so expensive?
sentences.zh: 这就带来了我们面临的一个大问题：为什么香水仍然这么贵？

sentences.en: Even if you don’t buy perfume yourself, you will probably have walked through the duty-free section of an airport or perhaps visited a high-end department store.
sentences.zh: 即使你自己不买香水，你也可能走过机场的免税店，或者逛过高端百货公司。

sentences.en: And you’ll know that perfume doesn’t come cheap.
sentences.zh: 你会知道香水可不便宜。

sentences.en: A small bottle from a luxury brand can easily set you back €100 or more, and some even sell for thousands.
sentences.zh: 奢侈品牌的一小瓶香水很容易让你花掉 100 欧元甚至更多，有些甚至售价数千欧元。

sentences.en: But, if it’s just smelly water, why is it so expensive?
sentences.zh: 但是，既然它只带点香味的水，为什么会这么贵？

sentences.en: Well, this isn’t a sponsored message from Chanel or the tourist authority of Grasse, but there are some good reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不是来自香奈儿（Chanel）或格拉斯旅游局的赞助广告，但这里确实有一些合理的解释。

sentences.en: First, there’s the cost of ingredients. Some of the world’s most famous perfumes contain materials that are incredibly rare and difficult to obtain.
sentences.zh: 首先是原料成本。世界上一些最著名的香水含有极其罕见且难以获得的材料。

sentences.en: Take, for example, oud, which is a resin produced by a particular type of tree when it becomes infected with mould.
sentences.zh: 以沉香（oud）为例，它是一种特定类型的树木在被霉菌感染时产生的树脂。

sentences.en: It’s one of the most expensive raw materials in the world, costing more per gram than gold.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最昂贵的原材料之一，每克的成本比黄金还要贵。

sentences.en: And even things that seem more run-of-the-mill, more ordinary, like jasmine and rose, which are used in many classic perfumes.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些看起来更平常、更普通的成分，比如许多经典香水中使用的茉莉和玫瑰。

sentences.en: It takes thousands of petals to produce just a few millilitres of essential oil, and harvesting them is a delicate, time-consuming process.
sentences.zh: 产生短短几毫升精油需要数千片花瓣，而收割它们是一个细腻而耗时的过程。

sentences.en: And then there are the synthetic ingredients, which allow perfumers to create scents that don’t exist in nature, like the smell of fresh linen or a salty ocean breeze.
sentences.zh: 还有合成成分，它们使调香师能够创造出自然界中不存在的气味，比如新鲜亚麻布的气味或咸咸的海风。

sentences.en: These molecules can be incredibly expensive to develop, and some take years of research before they’re ready to be used in a commercial fragrance.
sentences.zh: 开发这些分子可能成本极高，有些甚至需要多年的研究才能准备好用于商业香水。

sentences.en: So it’s not so dissimilar to some pharmaceutical drugs, where the raw materials might not be expensive, but all of the research and development that goes into creating them is, so that’s what you’re paying for.
sentences.zh: 所以这与某些医药有些相似，原材料可能并不贵，但创造它们所投入的所有研发成本很高，这才是你真正为之付费的部分。

sentences.en: And, lest we forget, there’s the branding.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们千万不要忘记，还有品牌效应。

sentences.en: When you buy a bottle of perfume, you’re not just paying for the liquid inside, you’re paying for the name, the bottle design, the advertising, and the luxury experience that comes with it.
sentences.zh: 当你买了一瓶香水时，你不仅在为里面的液体付钱，你还在为名字、瓶身设计、广告以及随之而来的奢华体验付钱。

sentences.en: Perfume brands spend hundreds of millions on celebrity endorsements, high-profile marketing campaigns, and exclusive product launches.
sentences.zh: 香水品牌在名人代言、高调营销活动和独家产品发布上花费了数亿美元。

sentences.en: That little bottle on the shelf has been carefully positioned to make you feel like you’re not just buying a fragrance but a piece of a glamorous world.
sentences.zh: 货架上的那个小瓶子经过精心定位，让你觉得你买的不仅是一种香水，更是一个魅力世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Of course, not all perfumes are expensive.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有香水都很昂贵。

sentences.en: There are plenty of more affordable options out there, but the reason some fragrances command such high prices is this combination of craftsmanship, rarity, and clever marketing.
sentences.zh: 市面上有大量更实惠的选择，但某些香水之所以能卖到如此高的价格，是因为工艺、稀缺性和巧妙营销的结合。

sentences.en: And behind every great perfume, there’s a person who created it.
sentences.zh: 在每一款伟大香水的背后，都有一个创造它的人。

sentences.en: The term for someone who creates a perfume is a “nez”, a nose, and when you get to the top of your game, when you have the most highly-trained nose in the world, this is when you might be given the title of un “grand nez”, a great nose.
sentences.zh: 创造香水的人被称为“nez”，也就是“鼻子”，当你达到职业巅峰，拥有世界上训练有素的鼻子时，你可能会被授予“un grand nez”（伟大的鼻子）的称号。

sentences.en: Now, becoming a grand nez isn’t something that you or I can “apply for”, and it certainly isn’t something that happens overnight.
sentences.zh: 现在，成为一个 grand nez 并不是你我“申请”就能当上的，这当然也不是一朝一夕就能实现的事情。

sentences.en: It takes years of training, a truly exceptional sense of smell, and an ability to create complex, layered compositions.
sentences.zh: 这需要多年的训练、真正卓越的嗅觉，以及创造复杂、多层香调组合的能力。

sentences.en: It isn’t an official title, and there is no official list of “grand nez”, but it’s thought that there are fewer than 100 worldwide, with some estimates putting it at as little as 30.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个官方头衔，也没有官方的“grand nez”名单，但据认为全球不到 100 人，有些估计甚至认为只有 30 人左右。

sentences.en: In fact, saying “worldwide” is a little deceptive, as most of them are in France, split between Paris and Grasse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，说“全球”有点虚晃一枪，因为他们大多数都在法国，分散在巴黎和格拉斯。

sentences.en: And something that might be surprising, is that despite the fact that most perfume has historically been made for women, the industry of being a “nez”, and especially the “grand nez” at the very top of the profession, has traditionally been a male one.
sentences.zh: 可能令人惊讶的一点是，尽管历史上大多数香水都是为女性制造的，“nez”这个职业，尤其是处于行业顶端的“grand nez”，传统上一直是一个由男性主导的领域。

sentences.en: Now, this is changing; women’s perfume has gone from being around 85% of the market to 60%, and there are more women getting involved in the business of making perfume, but it is a curiosity that it has traditionally been the noses of men that have decided what the noses of women would enjoy.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种情况正在改变；女性香水从占市场的 85% 左右下降到 60%，越来越多的女性参与到香水制造的生意中，但传统上一直是男人的鼻子在决定女人的鼻子会喜欢什么，这确实是一件奇妙的事。

sentences.en: Now, before we end this perfumed journey, I want to leave you with some interesting facts about the life of a “nez”.
sentences.zh: 好了，在我们结束这段芳香之旅前，我想和大家分享一些关于“nez”生活的有趣事实。

sentences.en: Firstly, although you might imagine one of these “grand nez” to always smell fantastic, and to be covered head to toe with fragrance when they come into the office in the morning, they aren’t.
sentences.zh: 首先，虽然你可能会想象这些“grand nez”闻起来总是棒极了，早晨一进办公室就从头到脚喷满香水，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They have to avoid strong smells, precisely so that there is nothing interfering with their ability to detect the subtle nuances of different smells.
sentences.zh: 他们必须避开强烈的气味，恰恰是为了不让任何东西干扰他们辨别不同气味细微差别的能力。

sentences.en: Secondly, and on a related point and bucking the French stereotype, they must avoid garlic, as well as other spicy foods, because they too mean that you can’t differentiate as well between scents.
sentences.zh: 其次，顺着这个话题，打破法国人的刻板印象，他们必须避开大蒜以及其他辛辣食物，因为这些食物同样意味着你无法很好地分辨出气味之间的差异。

sentences.en: And further defying certain French stereotypes, most grand nez also steer clear of coffee, cigarettes and alcohol for the same reasons.
sentences.zh: 为了进一步打破某些法国人的刻板印象，大多数 grand nez 出于同样的原因也对咖啡、香烟和酒精敬而远之。

sentences.en: Thirdly, apparently, they do most of their hardest work in the morning.
sentences.zh: 第三，显然，他们最艰难的工作大都在早晨完成。

sentences.en: This isn’t some productivity hack, but rather that everyone’s sense of smell is most sensitive in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么提高生产力的诀窍，而是因为每个人的嗅觉在早晨最为灵敏。

sentences.en: And if your job relies on your sense of smell, well, I guess it does make sense to do the most important work in the morning.
sentences.zh: 如果你的工作依赖于嗅觉，嗯，我想把最重要的工作放在早晨做确实说得通。

sentences.en: And while the job might seem glamorous, it’s also incredibly challenging.
sentences.zh: 虽然这份工作看起来光鲜亮丽，但它也极具挑战性。

sentences.en: The competition is fierce, and trends in the perfume industry change rapidly.
sentences.zh: 竞争异常激烈，香水行业的潮流瞬息万变。

sentences.en: One year, everyone wants fresh, citrusy scents; the next, warm and woody fragrances are in demand.
sentences.zh: 有一年，大家都想要清新、柑橘调的香水；而下一年，温暖、木质调的香水又成了抢手货。

sentences.en: A perfumer has to be both an artist and a scientist, constantly experimenting, refining, and adapting.
sentences.zh: 调香师必须兼具艺术家和科学家的双重身份，不断地试验、精炼和适应。

sentences.en: But if they succeed, their work can last for generations.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们成功了，他们的作品可以流传好几代人。

sentences.en: Some of the most famous perfumes in history were created decades ago and are still bestsellers today.
sentences.zh: 历史上一些最著名的香水是几十年前创造的，至今仍是畅销产品。

sentences.en: Chanel No. 5, for example, has been around for over a hundred years and remains one of the most iconic fragrances in the world.
sentences.zh: 例如，香奈儿 5 号（Chanel No. 5）已经存在了一个多世纪，依然是世界上最具标志性的香水之一。

sentences.en: So the next time you walk past a perfume counter and catch a familiar scent in the air, pause for a moment to think about the journey it took to get there.
sentences.zh: 所以，下次当你走过香水柜台，在空气中捕捉到熟悉的香味时，不妨停顿片刻，想想它经历怎样的旅程才来到这里。

sentences.en: From the ancient temples of Mesopotamia to the laboratories of modern perfumers, from the rarest natural ingredients to the synthetic molecules designed to mimic them, perfume is much more than just a pleasant smell.
sentences.zh: 从美索不达米亚的古代神庙到现代调香师的实验室，从最稀有的天然成分到旨在模仿它们的合成分子，香水远不止是一种令人愉悦的气味。

sentences.en: It’s history, it’s science, it’s art. And above all, it’s something that connects us, across cultures, across time, through the power of scent.
sentences.zh: 它是历史，是科学，是艺术。最重要的是，它是一种通过嗅觉的力量将我们跨越文化、跨越时间连接在一起的事物。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the curious history of perfume.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于香水奇妙历史的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，也希望你学到了新的知识。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的头脑畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
